function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal instruction or authorization that gives someone (usually a financial institution or service provider) the right to act on behalf of another party—typically a client or investor. Think of it as a “power‑of‑attorney” for specific financial activities. ### Key points | Aspect | What it means | |--------|---------------| | **Purpose** | Allows a third party to execute transactions, manage assets, or perform other duties without the client having to do it personally. | | **Typical users** | Investors, pension funds, insurance companies, or any entity that needs a trusted intermediary to handle complex or frequent transactions. | | **Common types** | • **Active** – the mandate is currently in force and can be used.
• **Pending** – the mandate has been requested but not yet approved or activated.
• **Inactive** – the mandate has expired, been cancelled, or is otherwise not usable. | ### Example Suppose you’re a private investor who wants a wealth‑management firm to buy and sell securities on your behalf. You sign a **mandate** that: 1. Grants the firm the authority to trade in your portfolio. 2. Specifies the limits (e.g., maximum trade size, risk tolerance). 3. Sets the duration (e.g., 12 months). Once signed, the firm can execute trades within those parameters without needing your approval for each transaction. --- In short, a mandate is a legally binding authorization that lets a designated party act on your behalf in financial matters.
